name: Mangools
subcategory: keyword research, backlinks and rank tracking
tagline: Organize keyword ideas and low-volume rank checks from a compliant data provider

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 100 keyword lookups/24 hours; up to 200 imported keywords per lookup; 200 tracked keywords; weekly rank updates.
tiers.notes: Usage limits are shared with added subusers.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: 500 keyword lookups/24 hours; up to 700 imported keywords per lookup; 700 tracked keywords; weekly rank updates.
tiers.notes: Usage limits are shared with added subusers.

tiers.name: Agency
tiers.limits: 1,200 keyword lookups/24 hours; up to 700 imported keywords per lookup; 1,500 tracked keywords; daily rank updates.
tiers.notes: Usage limits are shared with added subusers.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 keyword lookups/24 hours (15 related + 5 competitor keywords per lookup); a separate 10-day trial includes 10 tracked keywords
pricing.hiddenCosts: The optional AI Search Watcher PRO bundle adds $12/month or $7.80/month on annual billing; extra seats are available, but the current public seat price is not shown.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Mangools, organize keyword ideas and low-volume rank checks from a compliant data provider. The hard boundary is bundled keyword, serp, backlink, and competitor data with polished simplicity, plus proprietary web index and data acquisition.
coreLoopDIY: Organize keyword ideas, track a user-supplied keyword set with low-volume rank checks from a compliant data provider, and show trends without pretending to recreate a commercial web index.
requirements: approved search-data API or manual imports
whatYouLose: bundled keyword, SERP, backlink, and competitor data with polished simplicity
moatNotes: proprietary web index and data acquisition
ongoingBurden: proxy and API costs, crawl freshness, geolocation, anti-bot rules, keyword normalization, storage, and data QA
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Mangools because customers pay for a continuously refreshed web-scale dataset whose collection cost dwarfs the dashboard around it. The recurring cost buys proxy and API costs, crawl freshness, geolocation, anti-bot rules, keyword normalization, storage, and data QA, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: SerpBear
priorArt.desc: Open-source search ranking tracker for owned keyword sets.

alternatives.name: OpenSEO
alternatives.desc: Keyword ideas, clusters and location-aware rank checks in one container; the data meter belongs to DataForSEO.

facts.install: Clone the repository, supply environment variables, and run the documented Docker-based web/database deployment
facts.engines: Uses DataForSEO for keyword, SERP, backlink, and related SEO datasets; it also exposes MCP/agent integrations for compatible coding assistants.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, audits, issue results, tracked keywords, and historical observations live in the operator-controlled application database; keyword and SERP requests sent through DataForSEO leave the server and are retained/billed under that provider's account terms.
facts.gapVsPaid: OpenSEO still depends on metered DataForSEO data and lacks Mangools' polished proprietary keyword database, difficulty scoring, backlink index experience, and effortless hosted workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert needs Docker, a database, authentication and email configuration, plus a funded DataForSEO account and API credentials, the rank tracker is not actually zero-cost to operate.

alternatives.name: SEO Panel
alternatives.desc: A dated but maintained SEO control panel: keyword positions, suggestions and reports, with all the glamour of PHP admin software.

facts.install: Upload the PHP application to a web server, create a MySQL database, and complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Sites, users, keyword positions, audit results, reports, logs, and plugin configuration live in the configured MySQL/MariaDB database; application code, cached files, exports, and configuration remain on the PHP host.
facts.gapVsPaid: SEO Panel's dated interface, brittle search-engine scraping, manual scheduling, keyword discovery, backlink data, and report polish lag far behind Mangools.
facts.setupBlocker: The first hurdle is a traditional PHP/MySQL deployment with writable directories and cron jobs; after that, search-engine changes and third-party plugins make maintenance much more manual than Seobility.

alternatives.name: SerpBear
alternatives.desc: Rank tracking with history, alerts and Google Ads ideas; not five mangoes, but it covers the edible parts.

facts.install: Deploy its Docker image/Compose stack, a Node build, or a supported serverless host
facts.engines: Rank checks can use configured SERP APIs or proxies such as SerpApi, SearchApi, HasData, ValueSERP, Serper and related providers; Google Search Console and Google Ads can add owned-site and keyword data.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, keywords, rank history, tags, users, and settings live in a persistent SQLite database and deployment volume; configured rank-data providers receive each query sent through them.
facts.gapVsPaid: SerpBear is primarily a rank tracker and lacks Mangools' integrated keyword research, difficulty metrics, SERP analysis, backlink exploration, and domain profiling.
facts.setupBlocker: The first real obstacle is choosing and funding a working SERP API or maintaining proxies after deployment; the historically free scraper routes documented by the project are not reliably zero-cost anymore.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Serposcope
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Still turns up in every free-rank-tracker list; archived in 2024 and untouched since January 2022.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a small owned-keyword tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Mangools in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Playwright, and a small React frontend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize keyword ideas, track a user-supplied keyword set with low-volume rank checks from a compliant data provider, and show trends without pretending to recreate a commercial web index.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create projects with domains, keywords, target country, language, device, and tags.
Fetch rankings only through the configured compliant API and enforce a daily budget.
Store raw result snapshots and normalized positions so every chart is auditable.
Display current rank, movement, best rank, URL changes, and a compact SERP history.
Import backlink and keyword files from third-party tools without claiming independent coverage.
Add scheduled runs, failure alerts, CSV export, retention settings, and database backups.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out building a general web crawler or backlink index.
Deliberately leave out circumventing search-engine access controls.
Deliberately leave out traffic estimates presented as observed first-party data.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
